precepts.text: Aaron and his sons were anointed and sanctified to minister in the priest's office, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.
precepts.point: Aaron was consecrated and anointed to minister in the priest's office, and his sons were clothed and anointed as their father, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

precepts.why:
The Levitical priesthood was established in Aaron and his sons. “thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him; that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.” His sons were clothed with coats and anointed “as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office: for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.”

Because Aaron and his sons were sanctified for that office, certain things were consecrated that the rest of Israel could not touch, and even a priest “having his uncleanness upon him” could not go unto the holy things, lest that soul be cut off from the presence of the Most High. The anointing set them apart, and the holy things were kept apart with them.

precepts.text: The thing that dieth of itself may be given to the stranger or sold to an alien, for thou art an holy people; the law marks the difference between Israel and the nations.
precepts.point: That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith. That same law elsewhere says to give such a thing unto the stranger or sell it to an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: these laws were given to Israel alone, and the other nations may eat those things because they are not the holy people. There is no equality in that.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

precepts.why:
“That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith.” The same law elsewhere shows what was to be done with such a thing: “Ye shall not eat of any thing that dieth of itself: thou shalt give it unto the stranger that is in thy gates, that he may eat it; or thou mayest sell it unto an alien: for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God.”

These laws were given to Israel alone. The other nations may eat those things because they are not the holy people; Israel may not, because “thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God.” The law marks the difference between Israel and the nations. There is no equality in that.

points: No stranger may eat of the holy thing, neither a sojourner of the priest nor an hired servant. But the soul the priest buys with his money, and he that is born in his house, they eat of his meat, because they are joined to the priest's household.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: The priest's daughter married unto a stranger may not eat of the offering of the holy things; but if she is a widow or divorced and has no child, and is returned unto her father's house as in her youth, she eats of her father's meat, because she returns to her father's covering.
A woman was commonly under her father's covering until she came under a husband's. The independent woman was not birthed from the Bible; she was birthed from Babylon.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: He that eats of the holy thing unwittingly adds the fifth part unto it and gives it to the priest with the holy thing; the priests must not suffer the children of Israel to bear the iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: Whatever offering is brought for a vow or a freewill offering must be a male without blemish, of the beeves, of the sheep, or of the goats. Beeves goes to the ox and that family, the oxen and bulls.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: Blind, broken, maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, shall not be offered unto the Lord. Scurvy is just having scratches; these offerings could have no scratches and no bruises, nothing bruised or crushed or broken or cut.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: Neither from a stranger's hand shall ye offer the bread of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them and blemishes be in them; they shall not be accepted for you.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: When a bullock or a sheep or a goat is brought forth, it shall be seven days under the dam. The dam is that animal's mother; the young must stay under its mother seven days, and from the eighth day it is accepted for an offering.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: Whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day. And the sacrifice of thanksgiving is eaten the same day; none of it is left until the morrow.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: Therefore shall ye keep my commandments and do them: neither shall ye profane my holy name, but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: I am the Lord which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. The Most High brought Israel out of the land of Egypt to be their God; that is the foundation the commandments stand on.
